I inspected your request and found no attached data or source files. I cannot produce a precise renewal percentage without the underlying numbers. (Stated uncertainty: I don’t have the data needed to compute an exact value.)

What I need to compute the precise renewal rate
- Number of customers (or contracts/subscriptions) who were up for renewal during last quarter (the denominator).
- Number of those who actually renewed during that quarter (the numerator).
- Any rules you use for edge cases (auto-renewals, mid‑period upgrades/cancellations, prorated renewals, multi‑year contracts counted on anniversary, etc.).

Standard formula
- Renewal rate (%) = (Number of customers who renewed during the period / Number of customers up for renewal during the period) × 100.
Sources explaining this metric and common definitions:
- ChartMogul — “Renewal Rate” (how to calculate and interpret): https://chartmogul.com/learn/metrics/renewal-rate/
- Baremetrics — “What is Renewal Rate?” (practical notes): https://baremetrics.com/blog/renewal-rate

Example (illustrative only)
- If 3,200 customers were up for renewal and 2,560 renewed, renewal rate = (2,560 / 3,200) × 100 = 80%. This is only an example — not your actual value.

If you want me to compute it now
- Paste the two counts (customers up for renewal last quarter and customers who renewed last quarter), or
- Upload a CSV/database export showing renewals/renewal dates, and I’ll compute it and show the exact percentage and any assumptions made.
- If you prefer, I can also provide a short SQL query you can run against your database to produce the numerator and denominator. Which option do you prefer?
